sections.content:
Topics:
1) Introduction, Important PDEs, types of second order PDEs
2) Characteristic curve method, first-order linear equations solved by characteristics, the wave equation in 1D
(3) Boundary problems, separation method and Fourier analysis(partial proof), wave or heat equations with 1D bounded domain and boundary conditions,
(4) Laplace’s equation
(5) Harmonic functions, Mean value property, Maximum principle and uniqueness of solutions,
(6) Laplace’s equation’s fundamental solution and Green’s representation formula,
use Green function as integral kernel to solve Laplace equations, explicit formula of Green function on ball and half plane

~ I have attached the PDE textbook below for reference.

sections.content:
The content is mainly based on the L.C. Evans PDE book, Chapter 2-3 and with some extra stuffs:

1) Heat equations (Fourier transform, Heat Kernel)
2) Wave equation( Transport equation, d' Alembert Principles, Finite Speed of propagation, Energy method, Duhamel's principle)
3) Heat equation in Full space (Maximum Principle, Regularity of Heat equation, Heat kernel, Energy method, Duhamel's principle)
3) Laplace Equation( Harmonicity, Maximum principle, Perron methods, Green's function)
4) Method of characteristics( First order PDE, Conservation Laws)

sections.workload: There are 10 homework and some are challenging. However, if you encounter any difficulty in homework, you can directly ask TA during the tutorial session or email to Professor Jin to discuss your thoughts. Besides, Stack Exchange is your best friend!!!

sections.content: You will learn about the canonical types of PDEs and how to solve them. These are elliptical, parabolic, and hyperbolic equations with solutions via Fourier Transform, separation of variables, etc. You will also cover basic boundary/initial value problems as well as proving uniqueness and existence of solutions. Instead of teaching you how to solve a specific problem, he teaches you a very generalised approach to solving PDEs. This means the class isn't your ordinary mathematics class in HKUST. Unfortunately, this approach is also quite theoretical. We didn't actually see or solve a single PDE until halfway through the semester! Just so you get the flavour, we followed Andras Vasy's book mainly. This is a more advanced book that focused on 'distributions' because they yield derivatives of discontinuous functions. A cool generalised approach!
sections.teaching: Gunther was a good instructor because he has an extraordinary background. He has been teaching for many decades and it shows. However, he only writes on the board by hand and his handwriting is terrible. He is also a pretty research-oriented person, so he can't really tell you how to solve a specific problem. I enjoyed taking his class a lot because of his teaching style.
sections.grading: The grading was just fine. You have some homeworks every 2 weeks and a final exam. No midterm. The TA is told to grade leniently because our questions were very very very theoretical. He told us the answers in the tutorial before the homework deadline, so you should get full marks for the homework. The exam is set by the TA and was based on the homeworks. Only a small upper division class, so the grading was reasonable.
sections.workload: The workload was relatively light. Your homeworks were certainly challenging but there were no projects, midterm, or presentations.

sections.content:
Three main parts:

1. Wave equation, diffusion equation
2. Boundary value problems (separation of variables) and Fourier series
3. Harmonic functions, Green's functions

The first part and second part are very easy, particularly if you have taken an ODE course before. The third part may appear a bit intimidating at first but the tools are actually quite similar.
